A user with an offshore Delaware LLC and a non-US bank account says Stripe refused to let them open an account and accept payments. They called Atlas hypocritical and said they have used PayPal happily since.
A founder in Algeria says local credit cards don't work and receiving even $10 from abroad brings a day of questioning about the money's source. They see Atlas as a great fit for their country.

A Canadian company owner warns that the FAQ's tax obligations, such as US federal tax on 'income generated in the U.S.', are complicated and should be prominent. Apart from raising money in the US, they see no advantage, and think Atlas suits experienced founders who can afford good advice.
One commenter calls $500 a great deal for an LLC that comes with a fully vetted operating agreement suited to an internet company, plus a bank account out of the box.
Critic: LLC setup costs about $50, and bank accounts, Stripe accounts and AWS-type credits are free elsewhere, so charging $500 is 'kind of overboard.'

A Michigan founder filed their own LLC for $50 with a short form, got an EIN online in about 10 minutes, and opened a local bank account the same day. Still, they say Atlas's value is access to lawyers, tax help and the founder network, and is probably worth it.

Warning: if you live in your home state, you may still have to register the Delaware LLC there as a foreign entity and pay annual fees. California, for example, charges an $800/year flat tax, which can offset the convenience of Delaware.
A commenter says Azlo, the bank account provider behind Atlas LLCs, doesn't let non-US citizens open accounts for its regular customers without a US passport.

A beta user has no regrets: AWS credits saved them thousands. They faced the same issues as the original poster, closed the SVB account in month two, and moved to Capital One Spark with no minimum fees. They wish Stripe partnered with a better bank, but liked Atlas's filing reminders.

A founder says support answered within 24 hours, followed up proactively, and quickly helped them switch from a C-Corp to an LLC mid-process. After a messy prior Delaware incorporation with hidden registered-agent costs, they strongly recommend Atlas.
Unless you live in Delaware, you still manage the business in your home state yourself, with extra forms and fees on top of Delaware's. This user says Atlas 'only solves half the problem.'

One user had a good experience overall, but migrating to a new Stripe account was a big pain. They don't understand why Atlas couldn't attach to the existing account or migrate it, though separating pre-incorporation activity later helped with taxes.

A user of more than a year says SVB sucks but $300/yr isn't a dealbreaker. Keeping the corporation running costs them about $800/yr, and Atlas made filing their 2017 taxes trivial without ever speaking to an accountant.

An LLC founder calls the Atlas setup very pleasant. It shows a clear checklist of what you need to do or are waiting on, emails you throughout, and reaches out for extra ID verification. They would do it again.
A foreign founder who used Atlas last month has no regrets. The process took longer than expected because of their own passport and photo issues, but support replied to every email within 12 hours.

A non-US founder abroad found the $25/mo SVB fee annoying and had to migrate subscriptions manually. Still, Atlas was 'like having an advisor who helps you with every step,' and they highly recommend it for first-time founders.
An LLC founder says the Atlas process was simple, but there's a lot of state- and city-level legwork Atlas doesn't do. They add that Atlas doesn't remove the need for an accountant or lawyer.

One founder says support helped correct mistakes on both sides, with a real person to talk to, and a deal reduced the fees. Some UX was unclear at first, but Atlas compared favorably with a LegalZoom experience they don't recommend.
A commenter says Atlas is technically open to Russians, but it's common knowledge that 99% of requests get denied.

Atlas's default high share count can produce Delaware franchise tax estimates of around $90k instead of about $500, with no warnings, so non-investment companies must adjust proactively. This founder also calls SVB, Atlas's default bank, slow, with a horrible UX and frequent downtime.
